findings.claim: MATRIX ROW 3 — lock-heavy migration: ABSENT
findings.observed: Read tools/sbe_gate.py gate_migration in full (lines 900-1012): it checks only forward/reverse legs ran against a restore, a rehearsal_run_id, and before/after row counts. Read src/brothersbe/impact.py DETECTORS (lines 53-101): the only migration-adjacent detector is 'destructive-migration' (DROP/TRUNCATE/DELETE-without-WHERE -> irreversible), which says nothing about lock duration or blocking behavior (e.g. ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN NOT NULL, CREATE INDEX without CONCURRENTLY, a long-running lock that blocks writers). grep -i 'lock' across evals/run_evals.py and tools/sbe_gate.py returns zero migration-lock hits (the only 'lock' hits are about the telemetry file lock and check severity wording, unrelated). No detector, no gate field, no eval fixture, no doc row addresses this defect class at all.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a migration-receipt field capturing whether the migration was profiled for lock duration/blocking (e.g. a 'lockProfile' object with max lock hold time or a boolean 'concurrent-safe' flag), a gate_migration check that FAILs when a DDL statement matching known lock-heavy patterns (ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN NOT NULL DEFAULT, CREATE INDEX without CONCURRENTLY on Postgres, etc.) has no such profiling recorded, and a run_evals.py fixture planting exactly that pattern.

findings.claim: MATRIX ROW 4 — fan-out doubling numbers: ABSENT as an automated gate/eval test
findings.observed: Read tools/sbe_gate.py gate_numbers in full (lines 729-900): it verifies a pinned snapshot_id, that query and second_derivation are textually different, and that rerun.primary equals rerun.secondary. It never inspects grain (row cardinality) or join fan-out. The exact defect class ('the join that quietly doubles a number') is narrated as a worked example in docs/book/14-the-data-engineers-deep-dive.md lines 110-160, with runnable illustrative Python, but it is prose in a book chapter, not a fixture: grep -i 'grain\|fan.out\|fan_out' across evals/run_evals.py and tools/sbe_gate.py returns zero hits. Two independent derivations that BOTH fan out at the wrong grain and agree on the same wrong total would PASS this gate today: nothing here would catch it. This is closely related to, but distinct from, bypass rows 6 and 7 in docs/BYPASS-COVERAGE.md (alias renames and same-source derivations), which ARE pinned as documented UNCOVERED limit fixtures in tools/test_sbe_bypass.py (test_two_derivations_differing_only_by_an_alias_pass_which_is_a_limit, test_two_derivations_over_one_source_pass_which_is_a_limit); the fan-out/grain case is not even pinned as a limit fixture anywhere.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a run_evals.py 'numbers' case that plants two derivations sharing the SAME (wrong) grain-changing join, so they agree on a doubled total, and assert the current gate reports PASS -- pinning this as a named LIMIT the way bypass rows 6/7 already are, or (stronger) add a lineage/grain field to the manifest schema and a check that requires the second derivation to state a different grain or join key set.

findings.claim: MATRIX ROW 15 — timeout with surviving child: ABSENT as an automated regression test, though the defect was manually measured once and honestly disclosed
findings.observed: docs/KNOWN-LIMITS.md lines 490-497: 'a `sh -c "sleep 60 & sleep 60"` run under `timeout=2` returned in 2.00 seconds and left both sleeps alive... expiry kills the CHILD, not its descendants, because nothing here kills a process group. The refusal comes back at the bound, and a grandchild the command spawned may keep running, detached, after the wrapper has already said no.' This was a one-time manual measurement ('measured rather than assumed'), not a pinned fixture. I read src/brothersbe/evidence.py lines 489-501: `subprocess.run(list(argv), ..., timeout=timeout)` uses Python's default single-process kill, no process_group/preexec_fn/start_new_session/killpg anywhere in the file. I read the full test list of tools/test_sbe_evidence.py::TestAccessAndTimeout (lines 481-542, 4 tests): test_a_fifo_receipt_is_refused_in_bounded_time_json_mode, ..._text_mode, test_run_with_timeout_over_a_slow_command_produces_no_pass_receipt (uses `python3 -c "import time; time.sleep(30)"`, a single leaf process with no children), test_run_without_timeout_is_unaffected. None plants a command that forks/backgrounds a surviving child.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a permanent regression fixture: run `sbe evidence run --timeout 2 -- sh -c "sleep 30 & sleep 30"`, then assert (via `pgrep`/process listing, or a marker file the backgrounded child writes after a delay) that the grandchild is still alive after the wrapper returns -- pinning the CURRENT behavior as a named, tracked limit. If the release wants this closed rather than disclosed: run the child with `start_new_session=True` and kill the process group (`os.killpg`) on TimeoutExpired instead of relying on subprocess.run's default single-process kill.

findings.claim: MATRIX ROW 16 — fake CI env vars: dirty-tree forgery is COVERED and blocked; clean-tree label-forgery is an accepted, tested-as-a-limit gap, not a caught defect
findings.observed: COVERED half: tools/test_sbe_evidence.py::TestDirtyTree::test_a_ci_run_id_does_not_promote_a_dirty_run (line 306) confirms a fabricated SBE_CI_RUN_ID on a dirty tree still reads LOCAL-ADVISORY, never PROTECTED-CI. UNMITIGATED half: TestTheSoundCase::test_a_ci_run_id_on_a_clean_tree_reads_as_protected (line 245) proves the opposite case is a documented LIMIT: on a clean tree, ANY value an operator sets for SBE_CI_RUN_ID -- real or invented -- reads as 'PROTECTED-CI' with zero verification against an actual CI/forge API. docs/KNOWN-LIMITS.md lines 288-292 and docs/THREAT_MODEL.md (row 15, lines 260-270) state this plainly: 'nothing here can tell a run id minted by a CI system from one an agent exported into its own shell.' I traced ciRunId/trust_level usage (src/brothersbe/evidence.py lines 405-423, 829, 870, 1020): the trust label is display-only in `evidence show`; no gate_* function in tools/sbe_gate.py reads ciRunId to alter a PASS/FAIL verdict, so the blast radius of this gap is a misleading human-facing label, not a forgeable gate result.
findings.recommended_fix: Given the label carries no gate authority today, the residual risk is a human reviewer trusting a PROTECTED-CI badge that was never verified. If the release wants this fully closed: require SBE_CI_RUN_ID to be corroborated (e.g. by calling the forge's own API to confirm the run id exists and matches the current commit, analogous to the token-gated `sbe pr verify`) before granting the PROTECTED-CI label, and add a fixture that fabricates a plausible-looking run id on a clean tree and asserts the label is refused absent that corroboration.

findings.claim: No hypothesis/mutmut/atheris; a deterministic, seeded, hand-rolled generative test exists and is wired into CI
findings.observed: grep -rniE for 'hypothesis|mutmut|atheris|fuzz' across every .py file in the repo (excluding .claude/worktrees duplicates) returns zero hits. evals/test_no_data_class.py line 93 'SEEDS = []' with seeds only added via repeated `--seed N` CLI args (lines 94-96), feeding seeded_cases() (line 1164) which uses `random.Random(seed)` (line 1193, deterministic, not wall-clock-seeded) to randomly compose 1-3 field mutations per fixture from pools of empty/vacuous/placeholder/comment-only values and assert the corresponding check still reports NO-DATA rather than a false PASS. .github/workflows/brothersbe-gates.yml lines 140-141 run BOTH the deterministic default (`python3 evals/test_no_data_class.py`) AND the seeded sweep (`--seed 1 --seed 2 --seed 3`) in CI, so this generative layer is not vestigial. Ran live this session (default, no seed): '30 checks discovered from 4 registries in 25 module(s), 3737 scenarios run, 2 waived by declared exemption, 0 failure(s).'
findings.recommended_fix: No dedicated mutation-testing tool (mutmut) or coverage-guided fuzzer (atheris/hypothesis) is present. The hand-rolled seeded generator is a reasonable, deterministic substitute for the NO-DATA class specifically, but it does not fuzz arbitrary inputs (e.g. binary garbage, deeply nested JSON, adversarial unicode) the way a real fuzzer would. If broader fuzz coverage is wanted for the release, consider adding a bounded `hypothesis`-based fixture for the JSON-parsing entry points (load_receipt, the numbers/migration/ran manifest readers) as a supplement, not a replacement, to the existing seeded sweep.
